What We Do

Full-Service Maternal Fetal Medicine Revenue Cycle Management

Maternal fetal medicine billing combines high-complexity OB consultation coding, fetal surveillance procedure billing, invasive diagnostic procedure claims, and fetal echocardiography billing. PMEX manages every revenue stream inside your existing MFM practice workflow.

MFM Consultation Coding

High-risk OB consultations coded at correct E/M complexity from the clinical documentation.

Fetal Non-Stress Test Billing

NST (59025) billed separately per test with correct interpretation and supervision codes.

Biophysical Profile Billing

BPP (76818 to 76819) and modified BPP billed per component from the ultrasound report.

Amniocentesis and CVS Billing

Amniocentesis (59000) and CVS (59015) procedure codes billed with imaging guidance add-ons.

Fetal Echocardiography

Fetal echo (76825 to 76828) billed by complete vs. follow-up study from the echo report.

High-Risk OB Ultrasound

Targeted anatomy scan (76811) and fetal growth scan (76816) coded from the ultrasound report.

Common MFM Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Biophysical profile components not individually billed when the modified BPP was performed.

PMEX confirms the BPP components from the ultrasound report and bills the correct code for complete vs. modified BPP.

Amniocentesis imaging guidance add-on not billed alongside the procedure code.

PMEX bills 76942 (ultrasound guidance) alongside 59000 on every image-guided amniocentesis procedure.

Fetal NST billed without confirming the interpreting physician is separately billable from the facility.

PMEX confirms the professional interpretation is separately billable and submits the NST professional component correctly.

Fetal echocardiography coded at follow-up level when a complete study was performed.

PMEX reads the echo report to confirm complete vs. follow-up study and applies the correct 76825 to 76828 code.

MFM consultation billed as an established visit when the patient has not been seen in the prior 3 years.

PMEX applies new patient codes for every first MFM contact with a patient not seen in the prior 3 years.

High-risk anatomy scan billed at standard OB ultrasound level instead of targeted anatomy scan.

PMEX codes the targeted anatomy scan (76811) when the report documents the detailed maternal-fetal assessment that supports it.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in MFM Billing

MFM practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to BPP component omissions, guidance add-on gaps, and fetal echo under-coding.

PATTERN 01

BPP Billed at Wrong Component Level

Modified BPP performed (NST plus amniotic fluid assessment). Complete BPP (76818, $185) submitted instead of modified BPP (76819, $120). The study performed does not match the code billed. On audit, the ultrasound report does not document all components of the complete BPP. Recoupment risk created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the ultrasound report to confirm which BPP components were performed: a complete BPP includes fetal breathing, tone, movement, and amniotic fluid assessment. A modified BPP includes NST and amniotic fluid only. The code is selected from the documented components.

PATTERN 02

Amniocentesis Guidance Not Billed

Amniocentesis performed under continuous ultrasound guidance. 59000 (amniocentesis, $380) submitted. 76942 (ultrasound guidance, $85) not submitted. $85 per procedure in guidance revenue not captured. Occurs on every image-guided amniocentesis without a guidance billing workflow.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX submits 76942 (ultrasound guidance for amniocentesis) alongside 59000 on every image-guided amniocentesis procedure, confirmed from the procedure note that real-time ultrasound guidance was used.

PATTERN 03

Fetal Echo Billed at Follow-Up Level

Complete fetal echocardiogram performed for suspected cardiac defect. 76826 (follow-up fetal echo, $220) submitted instead of 76825 (complete fetal echo, $380). $160 per study under-coded from one code selection error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the fetal echocardiography report to confirm whether a complete or follow-up study was performed. Complete fetal echo (76825) includes all required cardiac structures and views. Follow-up studies (76826) are subsequent evaluations of previously identified findings.

Questions

MFM Billing Questions Answered

A complete BPP (76818) includes fetal breathing movements, gross body movement, fetal tone, and amniotic fluid volume assessment. A modified BPP (76819) includes only the NST and amniotic fluid index. We code the study from the documented components in the ultrasound report.

Yes. Ultrasound guidance (76942) is separately billable when real-time ultrasound guidance is documented in the procedure report alongside the amniocentesis CPT code (59000).

A targeted anatomy scan (76811) is a detailed first or second trimester ultrasound performed for maternal-fetal risk factors. It reimburses higher than a standard OB ultrasound (76805) because of the additional evaluation components required.

Fetal echocardiography codes depend on the study type. 76825 is a complete fetal echo. 76826 is a follow-up fetal echo. 76827 and 76828 are the Doppler component codes. We select the code from the echo report documentation.

Yes. MFM consultations are billed as new or established patient E/M visits by the MFM specialist, separate from the managing OB's global obstetric package.
